title: Artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support tool for personalized HCC risk stratification
summary:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer) is the most common malignant tumour of the liver and usually develops in patients with chronic liver disease that has progressed to cirrhosis. The incidence of the disease is rising steadily in Germany and worldwide, due to an increase in cirrhosis caused by fatty liver disease. Although medical researchers are gaining a better understanding of the processes that lead to the development of liver cancer, the disease is often diagnosed at an advanced stage when no curative treatment is possible. This is because there are currently no reliable methods to detect and treat the precursors of liver cancer at an early stage.
Our ARCTIC project addresses this problem using the latest artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. The aim is to develop an innovative AI-based diagnostic tool called TiPredict that can detect early signs of liver cancer and its precursors. A wide range of data will be collected from different samples, including blood samples, histological analysis of liver tissue and genetic information, as well as imaging techniques (e.g. MRI). Combining these data provides a comprehensive picture of the liver, showing the progression from 'healthy' to cancerous changes. The ARCTIC project is being carried out by a national consortium of leading university hospitals with specialist departments in hepatology, surgery, radiology and pathology, as well as experts in bioinformatics and basic research. The participating centres include university hospitals in Leipzig, Munich, Hanover, Berlin and Heidelberg. These centres contribute their specific expertise to ensure the highest possible quality of clinical and experimental data.
The close collaboration between clinical and basic research is crucial for the success of the project. While the clinics take care of the patients, collect blood and tissue samples and perform imaging tests, the basic researchers analyse all the data collected in the clinic to develop an AI algorithm and a liver model that can predict the development of cancer. 
The project consists of several phases that build on each other. The first phase will involve 100 patients who are at increased risk of developing liver cancer due to cirrhosis caused by metabolic abnormalities associated with steatoic liver disease (MASLD) or alcohol-related liver damage, as well as those who have already developed liver cancer. As part of any necessary liver surgery (either partial liver resection or liver transplantation), detailed MRI scans will be taken to identify suspicious nodules. Tissue samples will be taken from these nodules and the surrounding tissue during surgery. These samples will then undergo genetic, molecular and histological testing. The aim is to create a comprehensive molecular profile of these tissues and to understand their development.
At the same time, a total of 240 patients with cirrhosis whose characteristics indicate an increased risk of liver cancer are being sought. These patients will then undergo regular MRI scans for up to five years. MRI is currently the best way to detect the progression of liver disease and the development of liver cancer at an early stage, so that it can be treated effectively. We will then be able to use the results and data from this observational study to check whether the AI-based liver model we developed would have been able to correctly predict the course of the disease.
The ARCTIC project has the potential to transform the care of patients with liver disease. By diagnosing liver cancer and its precursors at an early stage, therapies can be
at a stage when they are most effective. In addition, the project will contribute to a better understanding of the processes that lead to the development of liver cancer. In the long term, this could lead to new approaches to prevention and treatment.

interventions.name: Volunteers in the TRAINING cohort: Patients ≥18 years old, which have alcohol-related or NAFLD-induced cirrhosis (plus/minus HCC), and have an indication for liver transplantation or resection.

Volunteers in the SCREENING cohort: Patients ≥18 years old, which have alcohol-related or NAFLD-induced clinically compensated cirrhosis without HCC with a life expectancy of ≥ 5 years. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
TRAINING cohort: Patients can be included if they:
-	have given written informed consent for participation in the study
-	have liver cirrhosis as proven by radiologic criteria and FS ≥12 kPa, stratified 1:1 by NAFLD or alcohol consumption as most probable causes
-	have an indication for liver transplantation or resection. 
-	have been screened for the TRAINING cohort and receive a screening MRI as part of the standard preoperative diagnostic algorithm. 
-	present non-classifiable hepatic nodules (LI-RADS -2/-3)
-	have biopsies successfully be taken intraoperatively from the imaging-predefined nodules as well as surrounding nodules not prominent on imaging (up to 5 LI-RADS -2/-3 nodules and up to 5 surrounding nodules)
SCREENING cohort: Patients can be included if they:
-	have given written informed consent for participation in the study
-	have compensated liver cirrhosis due to either alcohol-related liver disease or MASLD
-	meets risk criteria for the presence of unclassified nodules including at least one of:
o	liver stiffness ≥12 kPa by elastography
o	inhomogeneous multinodular liver structure on standard HCC surveillance ultrasonography or lack of assessability by ultrasonography due to obesity
o	diabetes mellitus
o	presence of cirrhosis over ≥3 years,
o	AFP levels between 6 and 14 ng/mL
-	present in gadoxetic acid-enhanced multiparametric liver MRI with at least one liver nodule ≥ 1 cm fulfilling LI-RADS -2/-3 criteria
-	have an estimated life expectancy of ≥ 5 years.
-	have successfully undergone MRI-guided biopsy of the nodule(s) as well as a biopsy from the liver tissue surrounding the nodule
Exclusion criteria:
TRAINING cohort: Patients will be excluded if they:
-	have a contraindication for undergoing MRI 
have liver disease other than alcohol- or NAFLD-related liver cirrhosis
-	have no histologic signs of cirrhosis in the explanted or resected liver tissue
-	have HCC or other liver malignancies in the liver
-	have not given written informed consent for participation in the study
-	pregnancy or lactation, or intention of becoming pregnant during study treatment. The ß-HCG value must be determined at each visit, unless the woman is menopausal 

SCREENING cohort: Patients will be excluded if they:
-	have a contraindication for undergoing MRI 
-	have liver disease other than alcohol- or NAFLD-related liver cirrhosis
-	fail to receive biopsy of at least one liver nodule and surrounding tissue
-	have HCC or other malignancies in the liver proven by liver biopsy
-	receive treatment with anticoagulants that cannot be paused during the biopsy
-	have increased risk of bleeding or with congenital coagulation disorders
-	have not given written informed consent for participation in the study
-	pregnancy or lactation, or intention of becoming pregnant during study treatment. The ß-HCG value must be determined at each visit, unless the woman is menopausal
